Prior to the recent elections, most investors were avoiding biotech stocks like the plague. Subsequent to the elections, biotech stocks streamed upwards. The NASDAQ Biotech Index rose 11%, while the S&P Biotech Index went up 18%. 
Analysts believe the upward trend represents a collective sigh of relief on the part of the healthcare industry, which was concerned about extensive drug legislation and artificial limits on the price of drugs. Indeed, Tarun Chandra wrote an excellent article explaining why he believes the biotech sector is now positioned to take off. 
Even though the climate has changed regarding biotech, investors need to remember that investing in biotech stocks is akin to gambling in Las Vegas. Big Pharma is not nearly as risky, simply because the big players have proven drugs in the marketplace and are reaping a profit. But there are many small-cap companies that are risking everything trying to get something into the pipeline. 
One biotech outfit that demands careful scrutiny is Kite Pharma Inc. (NASDAQ:KITE). Kite released its financial report for the third quarter of 2016 two weeks ago. Its revenue for the third quarter was $7.3 million. The company spent $57.3 million on R&D during the third quarter. The rate of cash burn for the same quarter was $54 million. Since Kite has $477.1 million in cash, cash equivalents and securities, analysts estimate the company can continue at the present pace into the middle of 2018.
